title: From pivot tables to SQL: Marketing Ops to B2B SaaS Data Analyst by fall 2027
summary: This plan turns the reporting you already do (campaign reports, HubSpot funnel data, attribution dashboards) into SQL-based analyses and published dashboards, ending with three portfolio projects and SQL-screen practice. Because past courses stalled around week three when work got busy, the first milestone is only three weeks long with a win in the very first session, every milestone ends in something you can show, and a 'busy week' rule (one 45-minute session keeps you on track) protects your momentum. Priority is practical, so you learn each skill by rebuilding real marketing and SaaS reports rather than through theory first.

milestones.title: Rebuild one of your pivot tables in SQL
milestones.whyItMatters: SQL is the skill every data analyst screen tests, and starting from reports you already build in Excel makes the first steps fast and familiar.
topics: SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY: picking rows and columns, like filtering in Excel
GROUP BY with COUNT, SUM and AVG: the SQL version of a pivot table
Translating an XLOOKUP-and-pivot report into a single query
Working in a free browser SQL playground with a sample leads table
milestones.visibleWin: You can write a query that reproduces a weekly leads-by-source pivot table you'd normally build in Excel.

milestones.title: Join tables to rebuild your weekly campaign report
milestones.whyItMatters: Real company data lives in many tables, and joining them (instead of chaining XLOOKUPs) is what analysts do every day.
topics: INNER and LEFT JOINs: combining contacts, campaigns and deals tables
Handling NULLs (blank values) and duplicates in joined results, using your HubSpot hygiene know-how
CASE WHEN: building your own categories, like lead routing rules in SQL
Moving to the free Google BigQuery sandbox, a cloud data warehouse (where companies store data for querying)
Saving queries in a GitHub repo with clear comments
milestones.visibleWin: A single commented SQL query in BigQuery that produces your weekly campaign performance report from separate contacts, campaigns and deals tables, saved to your new GitHub repo.

milestones.title: Portfolio project 1: B2B marketing funnel analysis
milestones.whyItMatters: A funnel conversion analysis is exactly what B2B SaaS teams ask analysts for, and it lets you tell an interview story straight from your current job.
topics: Framing the question first: which funnel stage is leaking and why, and what decision the answer drives
Defining metrics precisely, e.g. what counts as an MQL-to-SQL conversion and over what time window
CTEs (named steps inside a query) and subqueries to build the funnel stage by stage
Your first Looker Studio dashboard connected to BigQuery
Writing a one-page recommendation for a VP of Marketing
milestones.project: End-to-end funnel conversion analysis on a realistic B2B SaaS dataset: SQL with CTEs on GitHub, a published Looker Studio dashboard and a short written recommendation.
milestones.visibleWin: A public dashboard link and a one-page recommendation you could hand to your VP of Marketing today.

milestones.title: Portfolio project 2: SaaS revenue retention and churn with window functions
milestones.whyItMatters: ARR, churn and net revenue retention are the metrics SaaS leaders watch most, and window functions are the hardest part of most SQL screens.
topics: MRR and ARR (monthly and annual recurring revenue), new vs. expansion vs. churned revenue
Gross and net revenue retention (how much revenue you keep from existing customers, before and after upsells)
CAC and LTV (cost to win a customer and the revenue they bring over time)
Window functions: LAG, running totals, RANK and ROW_NUMBER to compare each month with the last
Cohort retention tables: grouping customers by signup month and tracking them over time
Partitioned tables and query cost basics in BigQuery
milestones.project: Cohort retention and churn analysis on a synthetic SaaS subscriptions dataset: well-commented SQL with CTEs and window functions on GitHub, a dashboard and a written recommendation on where churn is concentrated.
milestones.visibleWin: A cohort retention chart and an MRR bridge (new, expansion, churn) built entirely from your own SQL, which you can explain in two minutes.

milestones.title: Portfolio project 3: a public Tableau SaaS KPI dashboard for your resume
milestones.whyItMatters: Employers want a polished public dashboard linked from your resume, and Tableau is the tool most often named in Bay Area postings.
topics: Tableau Public basics: data sources, calculated fields, filters and parameters
Dashboard design: one headline question per view, clear labels, sensible colors
Combining pipeline, marketing attribution and revenue metrics in one executive view
Getting feedback from one colleague and revising
milestones.project: Public Tableau dashboard of B2B SaaS KPIs (pipeline, funnel conversion, attribution by channel, ARR and retention) on a realistic dataset, linked from your resume.
milestones.visibleWin: A Tableau Public link on your resume that a non-technical person can use to answer 'which channel drives the most retained revenue?'

milestones.title: Package the portfolio and rewrite your resume
milestones.whyItMatters: Hiring managers skim fast, so your repo, dashboards and resume need to show business impact at a glance.
topics: Cleaning up the GitHub repo: README per project, question, approach, result
Rewriting current-job bullets around the decision each report drove and the metric it changed
Turning each project into a 3-minute spoken walkthrough
milestones.project: A GitHub portfolio with three project READMEs and a resume that links to it and to your public dashboards.
milestones.visibleWin: A finished resume and portfolio link you'd be comfortable sending to a hiring manager.

milestones.title: Practice SQL screens and take-home walkthroughs
milestones.whyItMatters: Most data analyst offers depend on passing a timed SQL screen and presenting a take-home clearly.
topics: Timed SQL practice problems on joins, CTEs and window functions
Talking through your approach out loud while writing queries
One full mock take-home: a SaaS dataset, a question, 3 hours spread over the week, and a short slide walkthrough
milestones.visibleWin: You can solve typical medium-difficulty SQL interview problems in under 20 minutes and present a mock take-home in 10 minutes.

firstSession.title: Turn a pivot table into your first SQL query
firstSession.whatYouWillDo: Open a free browser SQL playground (no install) with a small, provided leads table that looks like a HubSpot export. Write three queries: list all leads from one source, count leads by source, and count leads by source and month, the same thing as a pivot table you build every week.
firstSession.outcome: You've written three working SQL queries and reproduced a familiar pivot table in code, in one sitting.

notCovered.reason: Nice-to-have that would add 20+ hours; SQL and BI are what entry-level SaaS analyst screens test. Worth adding after the first job offer.
More of an analytics-engineering skill; you'll see star schemas informally in the projects, and dbt is easy to learn on the job or after landing the role.

Cohort analysis is covered in milestone 4, but A/B test significance adds 10 to 15 hours; add it in the buffer weeks if you're ahead, since it's rarely screened for in marketing and revenue analyst roles.

deadlineFit: The milestones total 37 weeks at 3 hours a week, finishing around mid-June 2027, well before your fall 2027 target to start applying. That leaves roughly 12 to 15 weeks of buffer for busy work weeks, holidays or adding A/B testing basics, so a missed week delays you rather than derails you.
assumptions: Your 3 hours will be four 45-minute weeknight sessions; in a busy week, doing just one session counts as staying on track, and the buffer absorbs the rest.
You'll use public or synthetic datasets for portfolio projects rather than your employer's HubSpot data, so everything can be published.
You can create a free Google account for BigQuery sandbox and Looker Studio, and a free Tableau Public account.
Your SQL starts at zero; if you've written some queries before, milestone 1 can shrink to one or two weeks.
You're targeting analyst roles close to marketing, revenue or growth teams, where your CRM and attribution background is a strength.
